facts.Status: The farthest human-made object from Earth
facts.Speed: ~17 km/s (~61,000 km/h) relative to the Sun
facts.Note: Carries the Golden Record, a phonograph disc with sounds and images of Earth intended for any spacefaring civilization that might one day find it.

facts.Status: The only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune
facts.Note: Launched 16 days before its twin Voyager 1, on a slower trajectory that let it complete a Grand Tour flyby of all four giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

The first spacecraft to explore Pluto and its moons up close, then flew on nearly 1.6 billion km further to Arrokoth — the most distant object ever visited, a contact-binary relic from the solar system's formation.

facts.Location: Orbits the Sun-Earth L2 point, about 1.5 million km beyond Earth
facts.Note: Observes primarily in infrared light, letting it see through dust clouds and look further back in cosmic time than any prior telescope. Its halo orbit around L2 is unstable and needs periodic station-keeping burns.
facts.Trajectory data: JPL Horizons predicted ephemeris through August 2031 (station-keeping burns are not planned further ahead) — beyond that the position is held at its last known point while Earth keeps orbiting.
